title: RGB LED: Mixing Colors with PWM
summary: Harness Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) and additive color physics to generate millions of custom hues.

steps.title: Light Physics: Red, Green, Blue
steps.markdownContent: An RGB LED combines three tiny LED dies inside a single lens. By mixing different amounts of Red, Green, and Blue light, you can make any color in the rainbow!

steps.title: What is Pulse Width Modulation (PWM)?
steps.markdownContent: Digital pins can only output 5V or 0V. To dim an LED, the Arduino turns the pin ON and OFF hundreds of times per second. Look for the tilde `~` symbol next to pins 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11!

steps.title: analogWrite() Duty Cycle
steps.markdownContent: `analogWrite(pin, value)` accepts 0 (always OFF) to 255 (always ON). To make Purple, send Red=255, Green=0, Blue=255!

steps.title: Color Mixing Quiz
steps.markdownContent: What color do you get if you mix Red at 255 and Green at 255 (with Blue at 0)?
